I found a couple of useful guides here and here, but still ran into a few snags along the way. I thought I’d publish my configuration in case it might be useful to someone else (or perhaps even myself)

recent_posts.title: Perhaps Too Much Validation · Aspiring Craftsman
recent_posts.summary: I prefer code that only includes comments for public APIs or to provide explanation of algorithms. Code that is free of the use of regions, explicit default access modifiers, and unused using statements. encapsulating excessive parameters into a Parameter Object, avoidance of excessive use of attributes/annotations, and of course deleting dead code.

recent_posts.title: For Whom is this Container? · Aspiring Craftsman
recent_posts.summary: Some of the Messaging platforms in the .Net space have pretty rudimentary APIs. You could turn to one of the Conforming Abstraction libraries such as NServiceBus or MassTransit. But now you have a dilemma: Frameworks such as this tend to require a number of components.

recent_posts.title: Pragmatic Deferral · Los Techies
recent_posts.summary: Software engineering is often about selecting the right trade offs. The more you code, the more you’ll have to maintain. The Art of Not Doing Stuff, when correctly applied, can save companies as much or more money than building the right things. The YAGNI principle is very similar to the firearm safety rule “The Gun is Always Loaded”

recent_posts.title: Magical Joy · Los Techies
recent_posts.summary: The Command Dispatcher pattern is used to decouple a message issuer from a message handler. Many .Net developers have become familiar with this pattern through Jimmy Bogard’s open source library: MediatR. For earlier versions of ASP.Net MVC, I still see it as a worthwhile pattern to implement.

recent_posts.title: Nine Years Remote · Aspiring Craftsman
recent_posts.summary: When I first started working from home, attitudes were quite different than they are in today’s post COVID-19 world. Full time remote software development jobs were few and far between. Most employers that allowed working remotely full time did so due to factors other than a belief that it was more productive and cost-effective.

recent_posts.title: User Stories · Los Techies
recent_posts.summary: The use of User Stories has become fairly commonplace in the software industry. User Stories arguably owe their popularity most to the adoption of the Scrum framework. The Three-part template has become the defacto standard for authoring User Story descriptions. The use of software agile-planning tools such as Confluence, Planview, Azure DevOps Boards, etc., tends to greatly diminish the need from which the template originated.

recent_posts.title: NServiceBus.Extensions.Diagnostics 2.1 Released
recent_posts.summary: NServiceBus.Extensions.Diagnostics and OpenTelemetry packages are now available. The packages are just small wrappers around TracerBuilder.AddSource and MeterBuilder. addMeter so they aren't strictly necessary but maybe look a little cleaner. Metrics themselves are part of the System. DiagnosticsSource 6.0 release.

recent_posts.title: Building NServiceBus Metrics with OpenTelemetry and System.Diagnostics.Metrics
recent_posts.summary: System.Diagnostics version 6.0 brought support for OpenTelemetry Metrics. This means you can use these new metrics APIs in any application targeting .NET 4.6.1 and above. I wanted to try this new API out with NServiceBus metrics, to see how easy it was to bridge their metrics with the Open telemetry ones.

recent_posts.title: Activity Enrichment in ASP.NET Core 6.0
recent_posts.summary: As ASP.NET Core 6.0 includes a new Request Feature to access the current activity. We can add tags, baggage, events, or just generally inspect the current span. The Activity.Current property isn't the activity of the incoming web request, but something else altogether. If we want to start a new activity intentionally parented from this one, that's possible.
